- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-period, model often overshoots downward; adjust downward slope to match sentiment’s decay rate.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap next 3-day forecast at 10–15% below peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model often fails to mean-revert; apply slight downward bias (−1–3%) to mid-term forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.6), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean; apply 2–5% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or flat.
